hasEvidenceItems.description: The paper is a clinical association study and does not perform or report specific functional laboratory assays for the target variant p.His93Arg.

Multiple assays, including in vivo neuronal soma size/signaling in mice and in vitro biochemical PIP3 dephosphorylation in HEK293 cells, demonstrate that the H93R variant is loss-of-function. Although protein stability is normal, the variant fails to rescue the knockout phenotype and exhibits impaired catalytic activity.

hasEvidenceItems.description: The assay shows the variant has wild-type-like abundance, but the text explicitly notes that this specific variant (p.His93Arg) is an active site variant that is 'inactive without loss of abundance'. Because the assay measures abundance rather than enzymatic activity, it fails to capture the loss of function, leading to conflicting directions between abundance and enzymatic activity.
